Prepare for the session

Choose a clean, quiet place, settle your posture, and let your mind become calm. Prepare incense beforehand if offering it. Review the contents and decide how many repetitions of the great dhāraṇī suit your available time and energy.

The session proceeds through opening homage, refuge and precepts, repentance and aspiration, the great dhāraṇī, seven accompanying mantras, dedication, and closing homage. Follow the sections in that order.

Step 1 · Opening homage and incense

Recite the opening homage 3 times and the Dharma Realm purification mantra 3 times, then continue to the incense verse. Recite the incense mantra 3 times. Place the incense on the altar, read the incense aspiration, and recite the final homage to the Incense Offering Bodhisattva 3 times.

Step 2 · Refuge and the Five Precepts

Read the refuge sections for the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha in order. Recite each refuge mantra 3 times, read its accompanying aspiration, and make 1 bow at the end of each section. Then read all five commitments and their corresponding aspirations.

Step 3 · Repentance and aspiration

Read the repentance, then recite the dhāraṇī praising the purifying power of the Three Jewels 108 times. Continue with the aspiration, the invocations, and the prayer before the great dhāraṇī.

Replace the full-name and Dharma-name placeholders with your own details. If you have no Dharma name, use your full name alone. Read the praise of Mahāpratisarā Bodhisattva before beginning the great dhāraṇī.

Step 4 · The great dhāraṇī

Read the entire “Great Mahāpratisarā Dhāraṇī” chapter from beginning to end for one repetition. Recite it 1, 3, or 7 times according to your time and energy. Line breaks help you follow the text; they do not mark separate mantras.

Where the text shows a name placeholder beside “mama”, say the practitioner’s name. Recite clearly and steadily. Increase the counter by one only after finishing the complete dhāraṇī.

Step 5 · Seven accompanying mantras

Continue through the seven mantras of all Tathāgatas: Heart, Heart-Seal, Armor, Consecration, Boundary-Sealing, Innermost Heart, and Wish-Responsive. Recite each mantra 3 times before moving to the next.

Step 6 · Dedication and closing homage

Read the dedication to the Dharma protectors and recite the Universal Illumination Mantra 3 times. Continue with the dedication for ancestors, loved ones, and all beings.

Recite the mantra for increasing virtue 3 times and the mantra for making good omissions 3 times. Read the closing verse, then recite the homage to the ever-abiding Three Jewels throughout the ten directions 3 times.

Following the text

This edition presents English liturgy and Sanskrit mantras in Roman letters. The repetition counts appear beside the relevant texts. Follow the sequence and your chosen count, using the contents to switch between this guide and the complete ritual.

Benefits in Buddhist tradition

Mahāpratisarā belongs to the tradition of protective dhāraṇīs. Practitioners aspire to peace, the overcoming of obstacles, and the fulfillment of wholesome intentions. In this ritual, these aspirations accompany refuge, ethical commitments, repentance, and dedication to all beings.

Understand wish fulfillment together with self-cultivation, good conduct, and growing wisdom.

Editorial references: the Pañcarakṣā protective scriptures and The Great Amulet introduced by the 84000 Buddhist translation project; the practice liturgy compiled by Huyen Thanh.

Homage

NAMO NAMAḤ TATTVE BHAGAVATE TATHĀGATĀYA ARHATE SAMYAKSAṂBUDDHĀYA

Recite 3 times.

I bow to the Blessed One whose nature is reality itself: the Thus-Come One, free from greed, hatred, delusion, and affliction; worthy of offerings from gods and humans; perfectly and correctly awakened.

3 times.

Purification of the Dharma Realm

OṂ RAṂ

Recite 3 times.

Lighting incense

Incense smoke takes form,
Pervading the three realms.
The five aggregates become pure;
The three poisons naturally subside.

OṂ DHARMA-DHĀTU ANUGATA SVĀHĀ

Recite 3 times.

Place the incense on the altar, then recite the incense aspiration.

With a heart of reverence,
I send this cloud of incense
Throughout the ten directions
As an offering to the Three Jewels.
May I uphold the path throughout my life,
Doing good according to my true nature.
Together with all beings in the Dharma Realm,
I seek the compassionate protection of the Buddhas.
May the awakening mind remain steadfast,
And the resolve to learn endure.
May we leave the ocean of suffering and delusion
And swiftly return to the shore of awakening.

Homage to the Incense Offering Bodhisattva, the Great Being.

3 times.

Refuge and the Five Precepts

Refuge in the Buddha

I bow to the Buddha,
Perfect in merit and wisdom,
Shining like the sun,
Dispelling the darkness of ignorance.
Supreme healer,
Relieving countless sufferings,
Guiding all living beings
To the shore of peace.
With reverence I now
Follow in your footsteps.
May I leave all wrongdoing,
Perfect merit and wisdom,
And swiftly attain Buddhahood.

BUDDHAṂ ŚARAṆAṂ GACCHĀMI

Recite 3 times.

Having taken refuge in the Buddha, may I swiftly attain complete clarity, understand the principles and phenomena of all things as they are, leave affliction and suffering behind, and end the cycle of birth and death.

1 bow.

Refuge in the Dharma

I bow to the liberating Dharma,
The path of the noble ones,
Purifying greed, hatred, and delusion,
Transforming them into discipline, concentration, and wisdom,
Ending affliction and suffering,
Crossing beyond the ocean of rebirth.
With reverence I now
Follow this teaching.
May I swiftly leave birth and death
And realize pure nirvāṇa.

DHARMAṂ ŚARAṆAṂ GACCHĀMI

Recite 3 times.

Having taken refuge in the Dharma, may I always encounter, practice, and realize the true teaching of liberation. In this very life, may I swiftly develop composure, self-knowledge, awareness, self-mastery, skillful conduct, and concern for others.

1 bow.

Refuge in the Sangha

I bow to the pure assembly,
The authentic spiritual guides,
Who have trained body and mind,
Transcended craving and affliction,
Cut the roots of ignorance,
And raised the banner of liberation.
With reverence I now
Follow this bright example.
May I swiftly leave self-grasping
And attain purity free from sorrow.

SAṂGHAṂ ŚARAṆAṂ GACCHĀMI

Recite 3 times.

Having taken refuge in the Sangha, may I always meet authentic guides who have trained body and mind and transcended desire and affliction. May they help me overcome deluded pride, jealous contention, arrogant doubt, blind dullness, craving, and anger, purifying suffering, obstacles, and confusion in the six realms. May I live kindly, honestly, with moderation, integrity, and care for others in this very life.

1 bow.

Undertaking the Five Precepts

I undertake the training to refrain from killing. May all beings and I enjoy long life.

I undertake the training to refrain from stealing. May all beings and I attain our wholesome aspirations.

I undertake the training to refrain from sexual misconduct. May all beings and I abandon degrading desires.

I undertake the training to refrain from false speech. May all beings and I enjoy the peace of a truthful heart.

I undertake the training to refrain from alcohol and intoxicants. May all beings and I abandon confusion and ignorance.

Repentance, invocation, and aspiration

Repentance

Since beginningless time, through self-grasping and ignorance, I have been submerged in the cycle of the six realms: as a god, human, spirit, animal, hungry ghost, or hell being. In countless forms and dispositions I have experienced bitterness and sweetness, honor and humiliation, wealth and poverty, dominion and servitude, happiness and suffering. Obscured by ignorance, I cannot clearly remember it all.

Now, through a little good fortune, I have encountered the true Dharma of Śākyamuni Buddha, the Fully Accomplished One. He teaches us to relinquish self-grasping; remove greed, hatred, and delusion; cultivate discipline, concentration, and wisdom; do good and avoid evil; and purify our minds. Thus we transcend birth and death and attain purity free from sorrow. These wholesome practices must be undertaken now, without delay: life is brief, the body is vulnerable to illness and old age, and unexpected death may sever its stream.

I now resolve to follow this true Dharma. First, I repent all past wrongdoing, whether conceived in thought, spoken in words, enacted by the body, or caused through instructing others. The harmful karma thus created is vast beyond measure. Through the grace of the Three Jewels and their profound compassion, may my wrongdoing be purified. May I leave the lower paths, gain a human birth, encounter the true Dharma, and cross the ocean of birth and death.

Next, I vow to abandon every unwholesome deed, cultivate every wholesome practice, and train a pure mind, helping myself and others. May the Three Jewels always protect me, so that I swiftly transcend birth and death, attain unsurpassed awakening, turn the Dharma wheel, and guide all living beings.

Through the wondrous power of this dhāraṇī, may all anxieties, illnesses, disasters, and adverse karmic ties be removed. May the suffering of this life become peace; may I swiftly realize the true Dharma and transcend birth and death. Through the truth of these words, may I obtain excellent merit and wisdom.

Aspiration

I, [full name and Dharma name], recite the Great Pratisarā Dhāraṇī: the unconquerable heart-seal of the universally blazing garland, pure and radiant wish-fulfilling jewel. May the ever-abiding Three Jewels, the Buddha-Tathāgatas, great Bodhisattvas, noble assemblies, and Dharma protectors throughout the ten directions extend their compassion and protection. May I swiftly end afflictions, purify karmic obstacles, leave calamity and suffering behind, dwell in well-being, and realize the Buddha’s true teaching of liberation.

With my whole life I bow
To Mahāpratisarā Bodhisattva,
Whose body shines golden,
Manifesting eight arms
Bearing eight sacred implements:
Vajra, trident, axe, and sword,
Wheel and lotus,
A casket of Sanskrit scriptures,
Precious parasol and cord.
Seated upon a red lotus,
Emitting brilliant light,
Displaying spiritual power,
Please protect me.
May I leave calamity,
End affliction,
Subdue obstructing forces,
Cut through ignorance,
Bring forth a pure mind,
Practice the Bodhisattva way,
And attain awakening.

Dedication and closing homage

Dedication to the Dharma protectors

Gods, dragons, asuras, and yakṣas
Who come to hear the Buddha Dharma: be wholehearted.
Protect the Dharma so that it endures,
And diligently practice the Buddha’s teachings.
All beings who have gathered here,
Whether on earth or in the sky,
May you always regard humanity with kindness,
And abide in the Dharma day and night.

May all worlds remain peaceful,
And boundless merit and wisdom benefit all beings.
May every harmful karma be purified;
May all leave suffering and reach perfect peace.
Always anointed with the fragrance of discipline,
Always clothed in concentration,
Adorned everywhere with wondrous flowers of awakening,
May all live in peace wherever they dwell.

Universal Illumination Mantra

OṂ LOKA ALOKA KARĀYA SARVA DEVA NĀGA YAKṢA GANDHARVA ASURA GARUḌA KIṂNARA MAHORAGA HṚDĀYA ANYA AKARṢĀYA VICITRA GATI SVĀHĀ

Recite 3 times.

Dedication of merit

May this merit be dedicated to all. May our ancestors, parents through countless lives, and the departed rely on the virtue of the Three Jewels and be guided to a realm of peace.

May every member of our present family, young and old, gain merit and longevity, be free from illness and calamity, abandon harmful conditions, and swiftly attain right view.

May all beings always be happy.
May all beings swiftly leave suffering.
May all beings soon awaken compassion.
May all beings together attain Buddhahood.

Closing homage

And boundless blessings, all be dedicated.
May beings everywhere who are still submerged
